title: RunResult
description: The result of one run. Every run produces exactly one.

applied.description:
What delega applied to the run: the configuration file, which layer set
each request field, the environment, the deny rules and the context
mode. Absent when nothing is known. A refusal carries what was known
when it happened. See `docs/api.md`.

cleanup.description: Whether the processes started for the run are gone.

error.description: Why the run did not complete. Present unless `completed`.

permissions.description: The permissions that applied and what was denied.

provenance.description: The build and provider executable behind the result.

provider.description:
The provider that ran it. Absent only on a refused result for a request
that named none or an unknown one.

provider_notes.description:
Where the provider did not do what the request asked, or did it
differently.

schema_version.description: The contract version of this result.

session_id.description: The provider's own session id, for the provider's `resume`.

session_usage.description:
The provider's totals for the whole session through this run, when the
provider reports totals. For a run that started its session, the
session is the run.

structured.description:
The structured answer, when the request gave an `answer_schema`.

A JSON `null` answer is not representable: it reads back as absent,
because absent and null share one representation here. Report such an
answer in `text` with `structured_valid` left out.

structured_valid.description: Whether `structured` satisfied the schema. Present with `structured`.

timing.description: When the run was queued, started and finished.

usage.description:
This run's own token counts and cost. A field is present only when
delega knows the run's own value: a resumed run's provider may report
only session totals, and then delega leaves the field out or, for a
worker's follow-up, works it out from the totals the worker's previous
run reported. See `docs/api.md`.

worker.description:
The worker the run belonged to. Absent when no worker was created, such
as a refused request.

Applied.description:
What delega applied to a run.

`config` and `sources` come from the caller that built the request; the
rest comes from preparing the run. Each part is absent when it is not
known or does not apply, which `docs/api.md` spells out part by part.

config.description: The configuration file that was read. Absent when none was.

context.description:
The Claude Code context mode. Absent for Codex and when the run was
refused before it was decided.

deny_rules.description:
The deny rules applied (Claude Code only). Absent for Codex and when
the run was refused before the settings files were read.

env.description:
The environment the worker received. Absent when the run was refused
before the environment was resolved.

sources.description:
For each request field that ended up set, the layer that set it. The
keys are the top-level request fields and `permissions.*` and
`session.*` as dotted names. Absent when the caller did not say.

AppliedConfig.description: The configuration file that was read.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the bytes that were read, as 64 lowercase hex digits.

AppliedContext.description: What of the user's Claude Code context the worker saw.

instructions.description: Whether the worker loaded instruction files (such as `CLAUDE.md`).

settings.description:
How the user's and the project's Claude Code settings reached the
worker. `deny_rules` is the only mode today: the deny rules and nothing
else from those files. Free text, so a reader must tolerate values it
does not know.

AppliedDenyRules.description: The deny rules a Claude Code worker ran under: the files, never the rules.

applied.description:
How many rules were passed, after deduplication and adding absolute
forms.

files.description: The settings files that exist and were read, with their rule counts.

skipped.description: Existing local settings files that were ignored, with the reason.

named.description:
The names the caller gave with `--env` or in the configuration file's
`[env]`, sorted and without duplicates, whether or not the variable was
set. Names only, never values.

AppliedPermissions.description: The permissions that applied and what was refused under them.

mode.description: The mode that was applied. `read` when the run never started.

Cleanup.description:
Whether the provider process and its descendants are gone.

Serialized as `{"confirmed": true}`, or as `{"confirmed": false, "pids":
[...], "process_groups": [...], "reason": "..."}`. A confirmed cleanup with
leftovers cannot be expressed, and reading one is an error.

confirmed.description: True when everything started for the run is confirmed stopped.

pids.description: Process ids that could not be confirmed stopped. Empty when confirmed.

process_groups.description:
Process group ids that could not be confirmed stopped. Empty when
confirmed.

reason.description:
Why stopping could not be confirmed. Required when not confirmed,
absent when confirmed.

DeniedRequest.description: A request the provider made that was answered no.

request.description: What the provider asked to do.

DenyFile.description: A settings file that was read, and how many deny rules it held.

rules.description: The rules in the file, before deduplication.

EnvPassed.description: How many variables a worker received, by reason.

base.description:
Passed because they are in the base set (user, shell, locale, temporary
and base directories).

named_by_caller.description:
Passed because the caller named them (`--env NAME`, `[env] pass`) and the
environment holds them.

network.description: Passed because they are proxy or certificate settings.

provider.description: Passed because they belong to the provider being run.

set_by_caller.description: Set to a value the caller gave (`--env NAME=VALUE`, `[env] set`).

set_by_delega.description: Set by delega for the provider.

total.description: All variables the worker received. The counts below add up to it.

EnvWithheld.description:
How many variables of the caller's environment a worker did not receive, by
reason. Their names are not reported.

never_passed.description:
Never passed, even when named: variables that describe the calling
session, and every `DELEGA_*` variable.

not_allowlisted.description: Not on the allowlist and not named by the caller.

total.description: All variables of the caller's environment that were not passed.

ErrorDetail.description: Why a run did not complete. Present unless the outcome is `completed`.

kind.description:
A short machine-readable label for the kind of error. Free text, so a
reader must tolerate values it does not know. The kinds in use are
listed in `docs/providers.md` (Error kinds) and `docs/api.md`
(Outcomes): `invalid_request` for a request that failed validation,
other refusal kinds such as `cwd_unusable` or `limit_reached`, failure
kinds such as `provider_exit`, and `timed_out` and `interrupted`.

provider_exit_code.description: The provider process exit code, when it exited with one.

Layer.description:
The layer that set a request field. From lowest to highest precedence:
built-in defaults, the user-level configuration file, a profile file, then
the explicit values of the caller.

oneOf.description: The value is the contract's built-in default.
A command line flag of `delega run`.
An argument of the MCP `start` tool (or `follow_up`).

Mode.description: How much a worker may do in its working directory.

oneOf.description: May read the working directory; no writes and no commands.
May edit files in the working directory.

Outcome.description: How a run ended. Every run ends in exactly one of these.

oneOf.description: The provider finished the assignment and returned a final answer.
The provider or delega hit an error; `error.kind` says which.
The caller stopped the run, or went away.

The run did not go ahead: invalid request, a limit, or a denied
permission that stopped it.

Provenance.description: Which build and which provider executable produced the result.

build.description: The build identity, such as a source revision, when known.

provider_executable.description: Path of the provider executable that was used.

Provider.description: The provider CLI that runs the assignment.

SkippedFile.description: A local settings file that was not read, and why.

Timing.description:
When the run was queued, started and finished.

Times are RFC 3339 strings in UTC.

duration_ms.description: Time from start to finish, in milliseconds. Zero if it never started.

started_at.description: When the provider was started. Absent if the run never started.

timeout_secs.description:
The time limit that applied, in seconds. Same name and unit as the
request's `timeout_secs`.

Usage.description:
Token counts and cost, where the provider reports them.

In a result's `usage` every field is the run's own consumption, and a field
is present only when delega knows the run's own value. In `session_usage`
every field is the provider's total for the whole session through the run.

cached_tokens.description: Input tokens served from a cache.

cost_usd.description: Cost in US dollars, when the provider reports it.

WorkerRef.description: The worker a run belonged to.

name.description: The worker's name, if the request gave one.
